T: Sins in the street. Penance at the bar.
D: A small-time hood in Little Italy tries to keep his reckless friend Johnny Boy out of trouble.
P: Hit play on the jukebox and pour a round when Johnny Boy walks into Tony's bar.
S: charred and sliced, straight from the street feast
Grill Italian sausages over high heat until blistered, slice thick, toss with charred onion and capsicum, toothpicks and hot mustard.
Squid rings soaked in buttermilk, dredged in semolina and flour, fried at 190C for 90 seconds, salt and lemon.
Roast capsicums, peel and slice, marinate in garlic, vinegar and oil. Pile onto grilled garlic bread with torn basil.

as hot as Johnny Boy's temper
Fry garlic and plenty of dried chilli in olive oil, add crushed tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes. Toss penne through with pasta water, parsley and pecorino.
W: powdered sugar, straight from the street feast
Choux or yeasted dough dropped by the spoon into 175C oil, fried golden, tossed in a paper bag with icing sugar. Eat hot.
K: San Gennaro red wine with white peaches
the San Gennaro feast, poured from a jug the old Italian way

Chilled light red poured over sliced white peaches and left to soak, served in tumblers with the boozy fruit spooned in. Halve and stone 3 ripe white peaches, then slice thinly into a large jug. Sprinkle with 1 tbsp caster sugar and leave 10 minutes. Pour over 750ml light Italian red, such as Lambrusco secco or a young Chianti, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Serve in tumblers with a spoonful of peach in each. Eat the peaches last.

edition.cue: Hit play on the jukebox and pour a round when Johnny Boy walks into Tony's bar.

s.note: Blistered Italian sausage with charred onion and capsicum on toothpicks.
s.how: Grill 500g Italian sausages over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until blistered and cooked through. Grill 1 red capsicum and 1 onion cut into chunks until charred at the edges. Slice the sausages thick and thread onto toothpicks with the capsicum and onion. Serve with 50g hot mustard.

s.note: Tender squid rings in a crisp semolina coat with lemon.
s.how: Slice 500g squid tubes into rings and soak in 250ml buttermilk for 30 minutes. Mix 100g fine semolina with 100g plain flour and plenty of salt. Drain the squid, toss in the flour mix and fry in 190C oil in batches for 90 seconds until pale gold. Salt and serve with 2 lemons cut into wedges.

m.note: Penne in a fiery garlic, chilli and tomato sauce with pecorino.
m.how: Gently fry 4 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tsp dried chilli flakes in 4 tbsp olive oil for 2 minutes. Add 800g crushed tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, seasoning well. Cook 500g penne until al dente and toss through the sauce with a splash of pasta water and chopped parsley. Finish with 50g grated pecorino.

w.note: Hot fried dough puffs shaken in a bag of icing sugar.
w.how: Mix 250g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 1 tbsp caster sugar, a pinch of salt and 200ml warm water into a sticky batter and leave to rise for 1 hour. Drop teaspoons into 175C oil and fry 3 minutes until puffed and golden. Drain, tip into a paper bag with 60g icing sugar, shake and eat hot.

d.note: Chilled light red poured over sliced white peaches and left to soak, served in tumblers with the boozy fruit spooned in.
d.how: Halve and stone 3 ripe white peaches, then slice thinly into a large jug. Sprinkle with 1 tbsp caster sugar and leave 10 minutes. Pour over 750ml light Italian red, such as Lambrusco secco or a young Chianti, and refrigerate for at least 1 hour. Serve in tumblers with a spoonful of peach in each. Eat the peaches last.
